slides.title: 读出那个转折
slides.passage:
At first, the old kiosk on the corner sold nothing but newspapers and lottery tickets. Most people walked past it without looking up. Then, one rainy Monday, the owner, Mr. Alvarez, put a wooden shelf outside the door. It held twenty books, each with a handwritten note: “Take one. Bring it back when you’re done—or pass it on.”

At first, only a few children stopped. They picked up picture books, then chapter books, then books about volcanoes and football. Within a month, the shelf had grown into three shelves, and the kiosk had become a meeting place. Parents chatted while their children chose books; teenagers did homework at a small table Mr. Alvarez added beside the door.

The kiosk still sells newspapers. But now, when people say they are “just passing by,” they usually mean they are stopping for a while.
slides.highlight: Within a month, the shelf had grown into three shelves, and the kiosk had become a meeting place.

annotations.label: 01 · 之前 BEFORE
annotations.text: “Most people walked past it without looking up.” 报刊亭是“看不见的”：人们经过，却不会为它停下。

annotations.label: 02 · 转折 TURN
annotations.text: 一个书架和一张手写纸条，把一次交易变成了一个邀请。

annotations.label: 03 · 证据 EVIDENCE
annotations.text: “Within a month” 说明变化之快；一连串人物说明它成了新的场所。

annotations.label: 04 · 结尾 ENDING
annotations.text: “Just passing by” 现在意味着“停下来”；这个短语被重新定义了。

slides.takeaway: 事件很小；改变的是这个地方的意义。
slides.notes: 先读一遍，标出转折句；不要查词。

slides.title: 三个问题，沿着思维阶梯往上走

items.question: What did Mr. Alvarez put outside the kiosk, and what did the note say?
items.answer: 一个木书架，二十本书。纸条上写着：“Take one. Bring it back when you’re done—or pass it on.”

items.question: Why did the kiosk become a meeting place?
items.support: 把书架、纸条和人连起来。
items.answer: 书架给了人们停下来的理由；家长聊天，青少年在那里写作业。

items.question: What does the writer suggest by redefining “just passing by”?
items.answer: “Passing by” 不再等于“不停留”；这个地方改变了这个短语的意思。

slides.notes: 四个词块逐个释义；留一分钟做填空。
